description: Replace the free-text multi-Bot ambiguity prompt with one Server-signed interactive Slack chooser per ambiguous message, whose accepted selection starts exactly one execution for the chosen Connection from the original message, with durable decision authority, restart recovery, and bounded cleanup.

tasks.title: Extract the channel-root launch core into SlackChannelLaunchService
tasks.description: Behavior-preserving preparatory refactor (design Decision 6): extract the core of the private LaunchChannelRootAsync in SlackConnectionRoutes.ChannelIngress.cs into an internal SlackChannelLaunchService parameterized by project id, connection, message identity, sender, text, files, thread anchor, and pre-minted launch ids, so channel ingress and the later selection dispatch invoke the identical launch sequence (thread launch reservation, provider inbox route, attachment binder, InteractionWorkspaceProvisioner, admission, LaunchConnectionAsync with ConnectionLaunchOrigin). Project id is an explicit service input so a selection can launch in a different Project from the prompt-owner interaction route. All existing channel ingress call sites switch to the extracted service with unchanged outcomes.
acceptanceCriteria: The thread launch reservation, provider inbox route, attachment binding, admission, and LaunchConnectionAsync sequence run through SlackChannelLaunchService for every existing channel-root ingress call site in SlackConnectionRoutes.ChannelIngress.cs, with project id passed explicitly rather than captured from a delivering request context.

PreMintSlackLaunchIds deterministic identity derivation accepts the selected project id explicitly and is reachable from the service without a delivering-Connection request context (parameterized inputs only).
No observable ingress behavior changes: existing SlackChannelThreadIngressSpecs, SlackMultiAgentIngressSpecs, SlackChannelThreadReplySpecs, and SlackChannelAdmissionNudgeSpecs pass unchanged.
No duplicate launch logic remains private to the route partial for the channel-root path; the provider inbox still owns only raw Slack message ingress.
Relevant Server tests and the fast Server test suite pass.
tasks.output: packages/server/src/Mohist.Server/Slack/Services/SlackChannelLaunchService.cs with ingress call sites switched over, plus green existing channel ingress spec suites.
tasks.notes: Guarded by existing spec coverage; the extraction must not alter admission or nudge outcomes. Design risk entry 'Extracting the launch core risks regressing the ingress path' is covered by requiring existing specs to stay green.

tasks.title: Interactive chooser claim with durable original-message facts
tasks.description: Deliver the slack-agent-selection-prompt capability (design Decisions 1-3): extend SlackAmbiguousPromptRow/SlackAmbiguousPromptStore with non-nullable retained input facts (original sender, task text with all mentioned workspace-Bot tokens removed via a multi-mention RemoveBotMention variant, FilesJson, thread anchor, AmbiguityKind), an ordered CandidateReferencesJson snapshot of complete (ProjectId, ConnectionId) pairs from WorkspaceBoundBot or the workspace-wide thread-binding projection, and selection-state columns (SelectionState, ChosenProjectId, ChosenConnectionId, DispatchKind, pre-allocated identity slots, worker bookkeeping, FinishedAt/SettleReason) written by the same once-only INSERT ... ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING claim, with one additive EF migration including the (ProjectId, SelectionState, UpdatedAt) worker scan index. Replace the plain-text ambiguity prompt in HandleAmbiguousPromptAsync with one actions block of buttons sharing action id mohist_select_agent, one per mentioned workspace Bot when two to five candidates are eligible; when more than five candidates are eligible no interactive control is rendered — the once-only delivery becomes a readable text fallback requiring an explicit single-Bot re-mention, with no truncation, auto-selection, or pagination. The chooser message's plain-text field always carries the readable candidate summary and re-mention instruction, covering clients that cannot render interactive controls. Each button carries a SlackSelectionActionPayload (version, action, posting Project/Connection, team/conversation/original message ts, thread ts, ambiguity kind, actor, ordered candidate Project/Connection references, chosen Project/Connection reference, nonce, five-minute expiry — the issue-pinned Stop/Retry signed-action lifetime) signed with ISlackActionSigner over the Stop/Retry canonical form, delivered through the winner's outbox UserAction delivery under the existing stable dispatch reference. SlackThreadBinding, SlackMultiAgentRoutingCandidate, and SlackMultiAgentRoutingDecision carry complete Project/Connection references while preserving current routing behavior; the non-owner path (HandleAmbiguousNonOwnerAsync) keeps its existing guidance and once-only behavior, and the ambiguous message itself creates no AgentJob, AgentSession, SessionInput, or provider inbox entry.
acceptanceCriteria: A root multi-Bot mention posts exactly one chooser at the channel root; an explicit multi-Bot mention inside an existing thread and an unmentioned multi-bound-thread reply each post exactly one chooser in that original thread. Each 2–5-candidate chooser has one button per candidate plus readable text and no standalone plain-text 'mention a single Bot' prompt; the claim durably records RootMultiMention, ThreadMultiMention, or MultiBoundThreadReply; unambiguous messages render no chooser.

A message with more than five eligible candidates renders no interactive control and no truncated button list: exactly one readable text fallback is posted under the same once-only claim, requiring the sender to explicitly re-mention a single Bot, auto-selecting nothing.

The chooser message's plain-text field carries the candidate summary and single-Bot re-mention instruction in every case, so a client that cannot render the interactive controls shows the same guidance.

Concurrent per-Connection ingress, Slack event redelivery, and adapter failover collapse to one chooser via the once-only claim; a loser posts nothing; only the winner may retry an unpersisted delivery under the stable dispatch reference and a caller observing an existing delivery enqueues nothing.

Root and existing-thread explicit-mention choices are exactly parsed mentions intersected with workspace identity-bound Bots, deduplicated by Bot user id; unmentioned multi-bound-thread reply candidates are exactly the workspace-wide thread bindings. Both projections and SlackMultiAgentRoutingPolicy carry owning ProjectId with ConnectionId rather than bare ids, discovery remains workspace-wide rather than prompt-owner-Project-scoped, and interactive choices render only when at most five candidates are eligible; human mentions and other-Servers' Bots never appear as root choices; duplicate Bot identities collapse to one choice without added ambiguity.

The claim durably retains sender identity, mention-stripped task text, attachment metadata, thread anchor, AmbiguityKind, and ordered candidate (ProjectId, ConnectionId) references in non-nullable columns: store unit tests prove a claim cannot exist without facts or complete references and they survive to lookup; a claim lacking either can start no execution (surfaced, never reconstructed or inferred from the prompt-owner Project).

Each button value is a structurally valid signed payload whose constant-time HMAC verification succeeds for the posting Connection and fails for tampered Project ids, Connection ids, candidate ordering, chosen references, or another Connection's key; expiry is fixed at render time.

No AgentJob, AgentSession, SessionInput, or provider inbox entry is created for any ambiguous message at ingress (root multi-mention, explicit existing-thread multi-mention, and unmentioned multi-bound-thread reply scenarios).
The unauthorized-sender path still posts the existing owner-only guidance once, unchanged, with no chooser and no work.

Fixed-time fake-port spec tests cover root multi-mention, explicit existing-thread multi-mention, unmentioned multi-bound-thread reply, unambiguous, candidate-count boundary with 2-5 controls and >5 text fallback, fan-out, redelivery, winner retry, same-workspace candidates spanning Projects, non-owner, no-resources and the EF migration applies additively with existing pre-fact rows requiring no backfill.
tasks.output: Extended SlackAmbiguousPromptStore/SlackAmbiguousPromptRow with a new EF migration, SlackSelectionActionPayload with render-time signing, chooser block rendering in SlackConnectionRoutes.ChannelIngress.cs, and prompt-capability spec/unit tests.
tasks.notes: Design Decision 2 mandates buttons over static_select so the Go adapter contract stays untouched. Decision 1 keeps one durable record (no second selection-operations table). Expiry is the issue-pinned five minutes (same as Stop/Retry); retention follows the existing Slack event retention window — no new bounds are introduced.

tasks.title: Signed selection action handling with single-execution dispatch
tasks.description: Deliver the slack-agent-selection-action capability and the live-path core of slack-selection-execution-attribution (design Decisions 3-6, 8): add SlackAgentSelectionService.HandleAsync beside the Stop/Retry services, dispatched from SlackInteractionRoutes by action id mohist_select_agent while reusing unchanged operator authentication, runtime lease validation of the delivering adapter (stale lease -> lease_stale_or_expired before any processing), disabled-Connection check, and outbox UserAction reply delivery with ActionDispatchRef idempotency. The route passes a SlackLeaseContext built from that validated delivering lease to selection handling solely for prompt-owner current-policy re-authorization; it is never used for a different chosen Connection. The fixed-order acceptance pipeline: signature/structure (invalid_action), freshness (expired), context including the durable chooser-message identity, AmbiguityKind, and exact ordered candidate (ProjectId, ConnectionId) snapshot resolved from the acked outbox ProviderMessageIdentity and claim (stale_action), actor binding to the original sender only (unauthorized), recorded-decision short-circuit returning the decision view, prompt-owner permission re-evaluated via SlackConnectionAccessDecider under the posting Connection's current policy/allowlist/owner/live-member/channel-membership state using its route-validated current lease context (denial -> unauthorized, no mutation), candidate resolution and validity by project-scoped lookup of the signed ChosenProjectId/ChosenConnectionId pair (no global Connection-id lookup and no prompt-owner Project fallback; an absent/deleted selected Connection row -> unavailable, while a still-existing Connection whose snapshotted workspace-Bot binding no longer holds -> no_longer_valid), selected-Connection lease resolution (the chosen Connection's own currently active runtime lease read from the lease store for `connection:{ChosenProjectId}:{ChosenConnectionId}` and re-proven via ValidateRuntimeLeaseAsync; a missing, expired, superseded, or otherwise invalid lease returns a distinct visible unavailable outcome — never the prompt-owner's Project or delivering lease), selected-Connection permission separately re-evaluated via SlackConnectionAccessDecider under its current policy with a SlackLeaseContext built from that resolved lease, and executability in ChosenProjectId via the existing SlackAdmissionService setup-nudge / connection_disabled outcomes. When prompt owner and selected Project/Connection pairs are the same, one equivalent current lease-and-policy evaluation may satisfy both roles. Commit is a single compare-and-swap on the claim row to SelectionState Decided with ChosenProjectId, ChosenConnectionId, a durable DispatchKind (RootLaunch, ThreadLaunch, or ThreadFollowup), and pre-allocated deterministic ids minted for ChosenProjectId (PreMintSlackLaunchIds derivation over selected Project plus original message identity), then dispatch from the retained ambiguity kind and current selected binding: root multi-mention commits RootLaunch through SlackChannelLaunchService; explicit multi-Bot mention inside an existing thread commits ThreadFollowup when the selected Connection is already bound, otherwise ThreadLaunch through the same service under the retained original thread anchor; an unmentioned multi-bound-thread reply requires the selected binding and commits ThreadFollowup (missing binding -> no_longer_valid). Loser Connections remain no-ops, and recovery replays the committed kind without reclassification. Rejections are distinct visible notices updating the chooser message and create no selection mutation, winner, or execution resources. The Go adapter gains only test coverage for the new action id.
acceptanceCriteria: The interaction route dispatches mohist_select_agent to SlackAgentSelectionService with the same authentication and lease validation as Stop and Retry; a stale lease returns lease_stale_or_expired before any selection processing; the route passes the validated prompt-owner SlackLeaseContext for prompt-owner access evaluation; Stop and Retry outcomes are unchanged by coexistence.

Before candidate commit, the prompt-owner Connection is re-authorized through SlackConnectionAccessDecider under its current policy using its own route-validated current lease context; deterministic fixed-time tests cover policy narrowing, allowlist removal, live-member loss/unverifiable identity, and Bot channel-membership loss/unverifiable conversation between render and click, each returning unauthorized with the current actionable reason and creating no selection mutation, winner, provider inbox entry, Session, Turn, or AgentJob. When prompt owner and chosen Project/Connection pairs are the same, one equivalent current evaluation may satisfy both roles.

Each rejection kind (tampered/foreign-key invalid including Project ownership, expired, context, candidate-snapshot, or chooser-message mismatch stale; wrong actor or either Connection's current-policy denial unauthorized with the policy's actionable reason; absent/deleted selected Connection or missing/invalid selected-Connection runtime lease unavailable; still-existing candidate whose snapshotted workspace-Bot binding changed, or a missing binding/session when the ambiguity kind requires ThreadFollowup, no_longer_valid) produces a distinct visible notice updating the chooser message and creates no AgentJob, AgentSession, SessionInput, Turn, winner, selection mutation, or provider inbox entry; agent-not-ready posts the existing setup nudge durably and a disabled chosen Connection returns the existing connection-disabled outcome.

The chosen Connection is resolved by its durable and signed ChosenProjectId/ChosenConnectionId pair and authorized separately under its own current runtime lease resolved at `connection:{ChosenProjectId}:{ChosenConnectionId}`: a same-workspace cross-Project selection by a clicker allowed under both Projects' Connections and leases is accepted, a clicker denied under either current policy is rejected unauthorized, and a chosen Connection whose own lease is missing or expired is rejected unavailable even while the posting Connection's lease is valid; neither the prompt-owner Project nor lease is substituted for the chosen target.
A click on a stale duplicate chooser (outbox delivery retry) or a copied value, and a click on a delivered-but-unacked chooser, are rejected as stale with no resources.

An accepted root-mention selection launches the chosen Connection's Session in ChosenProjectId in the root thread. For an explicit multi-Bot mention inside an existing thread, selecting an already-bound Connection dispatches a follow-up to its existing Session, while selecting an unbound Connection launches and binds a new independent Session under the retained original thread anchor; the reply message ts never becomes a replacement root. An unmentioned multi-bound-thread reply dispatches a follow-up to the chosen bound Session and never creates a new Session. A prompt owner in another Project contributes no execution resource or project-scoped lookup.

Concurrent clicks on the same or different candidates, repeated clicks, interaction redelivery, adapter failover, and lost interaction responses resolve to exactly one recorded selection (CAS) and at most one AgentJob/Session/SessionInput lineage attributed to the chosen Connection; every loser or late clicker observes the decision view, never a second chooser or execution.

The decision is durably persisted with ChosenProjectId, ChosenConnectionId, DispatchKind, retained thread anchor, and execution identity pre-allocated for that selected Project before any dispatch, and no dispatch path may start work for the message outside that record (crash between commit and dispatch leaves the complete authority intact).
The same launch and admission services the CLI/Web use are invoked (no Slack-only execution path), and no other mentioned or bound Connection creates any execution resource for the message.

Fake-port fixed-time spec tests cover the full acceptance matrix (including prompt-owner current policy/allowlist/live-member/channel-membership denials, same-Project/Connection authorization de-duplication, same-workspace cross-Project success, cross-Project denial by either policy, selected Project rejection, deleted-selected-Connection and selected-lease unavailable outcomes, still-existing candidate binding-drift no_longer_valid, and no prompt-owner Project substitution), the concurrency/redelivery/lost-response attribution scenarios, root launch, existing-thread bound follow-up, existing-thread unbound launch-and-bind, unmentioned multi-bound follow-up, selected-Project provenance, and restart recovery without dispatch reclassification; Go adapter tests cover block_actions forwarding of the selection action id with no adapter contract change.
tasks.output: packages/server/src/Mohist.Server/Slack/Services/SlackAgentSelectionService.cs, three-way action-id dispatch in SlackInteractionRoutes, CAS commit in SlackAmbiguousPromptStore, launch/follow-up dispatch wiring, selection spec tests, and Go adapter test coverage for the new action id.
tasks.notes: Also satisfies the live-path requirements of specs/slack-selection-execution-attribution/spec.md (start-from-original-message, exactly-one-execution, durable-decision-before-dispatch, at-most-one-under-concurrency). Render-time authorization is never trusted; the Owner clicking another member's chooser is unauthorized per the strict actor rule.

tasks.title: Selection obligation worker: recovery, expiry settlement, retention, and docs
tasks.description: Deliver restart recovery and bounded cleanup (design Decision 7): a SlackAgentSelectionObligationWorker mirroring SlackAgentAppBindingObligationWorker that periodically resumes Decided rows whose dispatch has not completed by re-running the idempotent launch/follow-up dispatch under the committed ChosenProjectId/ChosenConnectionId, DispatchKind, retained thread anchor, and pre-allocated identity, never the prompt-owner Project, terminally settles committed selections that can no longer produce their execution (Settled with reason plus one visible outbox UserAction outcome under a stable dispatch reference, nothing executing afterwards), expires Pending rows past their five-minute expiry as expired, and reaps Completed/Settled rows older than the existing Slack event retention window (SlackProviderOptions.SlackEventRetentionWindow, 30-minute default — no new long-term audit archive) while never removing pending or in-progress operations. Update docs/slack.md and design/slack.md to move multi-Bot selection from planned to delivered.
acceptanceCriteria: A restart between commit and dispatch, including a cross-Project winner, resumes the selection in ChosenProjectId for ChosenConnectionId using the committed DispatchKind, retained thread anchor, and pre-allocated execution identity, producing the recorded execution exactly once and never a duplicate or prompt-owner-Project execution (fake-port recovery specs).

An unrecoverable committed selection (chosen Connection or Agent gone, lineage irrecoverable after repeated failures) is settled terminally with a visible outcome and creates no execution resources after settlement.
A Pending row past its five-minute expiry is settled expired, and a late click on it is still rejected as expired by the freshness check regardless of the sweep.
Cleanup removes only Completed/Settled records older than the existing Slack event retention window; pending and in-progress records are never reaped (spec scenario coverage).
The worker scans via the (ProjectId, SelectionState, UpdatedAt) index with bounded retry intervals and failure logging per the obligation-worker pattern; repeated resume attempts remain idempotent.
docs/slack.md and design/slack.md Status/gap notes present multi-Bot interactive selection as delivered, including the chooser and single-execution attribution behavior.
Recovery and retention spec tests plus the full Server fast test suite pass.
tasks.output: packages/server/src/Mohist.Server/Slack/Services/SlackAgentSelectionObligationWorker.cs with DI registration, recovery/expiry/retention spec tests, and updated docs/slack.md plus design/slack.md status notes.
tasks.notes: Bounds are pinned by the issue, not open: five-minute action expiry (same as Stop/Retry) and the existing SlackEventRetentionWindow for finished-record reaping; no new retention regime or grace margin is introduced.
